# ExtMergeJoin

## Description

General-purpose sorted-equality join. Joins a master stream (input port 0) with one or more slave streams (input ports 1..n) on a common key. All inputs **must be pre-sorted** by the join key. The SQL equivalent is INNER / LEFT OUTER / FULL OUTER JOIN with sorted-merge execution.

> **Name vs type:** the component is labelled *ExtMergeJoin*; always emit `type="EXT_MERGE_JOIN"`.

## Purpose & when to use

Reach for EXT_MERGE_JOIN when:
- Both inputs are large (slave > ~500k records or > 500MB) — heap exhaustion risk on EXT_HASH_JOIN justifies the sort cost.
- The data is already sorted upstream (e.g. coming out of a DB query with `ORDER BY join_key`, or already-sorted file).
- You need a streaming / low-memory join — EXT_MERGE_JOIN does no caching.

Don't use EXT_MERGE_JOIN when:
- Slave is small (< 500k records, < 500MB) — `EXT_HASH_JOIN` skips the sort and is faster on small slaves.
- Slave is a static reference table loaded once at graph start — `LOOKUP_JOIN` with a `SimpleLookupTable` in `<Global>` is the right tool.
- Per-record DB lookup needed — `DBJOIN` directly against the DB is more efficient than dumping the whole reference table into a CloverDX edge.
- You're comparing two sets for set-difference / intersection — `DATA_INTERSECTION` is purpose-built for that.

## XML template

```xml
<Node id="JOIN0" type="EXT_MERGE_JOIN"
      joinKey="$customer_id#$cust_id"
      joinType="inner"
      guiX="450" guiY="200">
  <attr name="transform"><![CDATA[//#CTL2 — see ## CTL2 contract]]></attr>
</Node>
```

- `type="EXT_MERGE_JOIN"`.
- Mandatory attributes: `joinKey`, `transform` (one of `transform` / `transformURL` / `transformClass`).
- Optional attributes: `joinType`, `slaveDuplicates`, `ascendingInputs`.
- `joinKey` notation — `<master keys>#<slave-1 keys>[#<slave-2 keys>...]`; each portion is a `;`-separated list of `$<field-name>`, optionally suffixed `(a)` (ascending) / `(d)` (descending). The direction suffix must match the input sort direction.
  ```
  $customer_id#$cust_id                               # field renamed in slave
  $first_name(a);$last_name(a)#$fname(a);$lname(a)     # composite, explicit ascending
  $customer_id#$cust_id_v1#$cust_id_v2                # one master + two slaves
  ```
- The CTL2 body is anchored in the `transform` `<attr>` CDATA.

## Properties

| Attribute | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `joinKey` | yes | — | Key expression. Format: master fields `#` slave1 fields `#` slave2 fields … (see `joinKey` syntax below). Number of master key fields = number of slave key fields per slave; the master key is shared across all slaves (same fields, possibly renamed). |
| `joinType` | no | `inner` | One of `inner` / `leftOuter` / `fullOuter`. |
| `transform` | yes | — | CTL2 (or Java) transform building the joined record. The Joiners transform template applies (see CTL2 contract). |
| `transformURL` | (alt) | — | External transform file. Use either `transform` or `transformURL`. |
| `slaveDuplicates` | no | `true` | When `true`, repeated slave keys all join with master. When `false`, only the **last** slave record at a given key is used. |
| `charset` | no | — | Encoding of the external `transformURL` file / inline transform source. |
| `ascendingInputs` | no | `true` | **Deprecated.** If `false`, expects inputs sorted in descending order. |
| `leftOuterJoin` | no | — | **Deprecated.** Use `joinType="leftOuter"` instead. |
| `fullOuterJoin` | no | — | **Deprecated.** Use `joinType="fullOuter"` instead. |

### `joinKey` syntax

`<master keys>#<slave-1 keys>[#<slave-2 keys>...]`

Each portion is a `;`-separated list of `$<field-name>`, optionally suffixed `(a)` for ascending or `(d)` for descending sort markers (must match input sort direction).

Examples:

```
$customer_id                                           # single-field, single-slave inner join
$customer_id#$cust_id                                  # field renamed in slave
$first_name;$last_name#$fname;$lname                   # composite key
$first_name(a);$last_name(a)#$fname(a);$lname(a)       # explicit ascending
$customer_id#$cust_id_v1#$cust_id_v2                   # one master + two slaves
```

Number of master key fields = number of slave key fields per slave. The master key itself is shared across all slaves (same fields, possibly renamed).

## Input & output metadata

Master (driver) on port 0, slave stream(s) on ports 1..n — each slave a separate input port with its own `joinKey` clause. The joined output is yours to define; the unjoined-master port mirrors port 0 and cannot be modified by the transform.

```
auto_propagated_metadata:   # joined output is yours; the unjoined port mirrors the master
  in.0:    <any — master / driver stream, sorted by joinKey>
  in.1..N: <any — slave stream(s), each sorted by its joinKey clause>
  out.0:   <you define — joined schema>   # transform() populates it
  out.1:   = in.0   # optional — unjoined master records (leftOuter / fullOuter only); pass through unmodified
```

A port-0 edge references your `<Metadata>`; the port-1 edge can ride the propagated master schema with no `metadata=` attribute.
- **Precondition — sorted inputs.** Every input **must** be sorted on its respective join key, in the same direction (default ascending). EXT_MERGE_JOIN does **not** verify the sort — if inputs aren't sorted, output is silently wrong. Common causes of failure: a `WHERE` clause that filters out the trailing portion of a sort, or a downstream step adding records out of order. Use `EXT_SORT` (or `FAST_SORT` for in-memory cases) immediately upstream; the `sortKey` of EXT_SORT must exactly match the corresponding portion of EXT_MERGE_JOIN's `joinKey`.

## CTL2 contract

Single entry-point function — the shared Joiners transform contract. The physical join strategy is sorted-merge; the CTL contract is identical across the join family.

```ctl
function integer transform()
```

**Call order / lifecycle:**
- `transform()` runs once per produced joined row.
- Return `ALL` to emit on port 0, an output port index to route, or `SKIP` to drop the row.

**Port model:**
- `$in.0` — master / driver record (port 0).
- `$in.1`, `$in.2`, … — slave records (ports 1, 2, …); null for left-outer / full-outer rows with no match.
- `$out.0` — output record.

**Idioms / keep in mind:**
- For `leftOuter` / `fullOuter`, guard slave-field reads with **field-level** null checks on a concrete slave key field, e.g. `nvl($in.1.region, "UNKNOWN")` or `isnull($in.1.region) ? "UNKNOWN" : $in.1.region`. Do **not** use whole-record checks like `isnull($in.1)`, and do not use sentinels (`-1`, `"NONE"`).
- Use fields from the correct port — slave-only fields read off `$in.0` cause field errors.
- Equality operators `==` and `!=` are null-safe; ordered comparisons on nullable values need guards.

**Minimal skeleton:**
```ctl
//#CTL2
function integer transform() {
    $out.0.customer_id = $in.0.customer_id;
    $out.0.name        = $in.0.name;
    $out.0.region      = $in.1.region;     // from slave 1
    return ALL;
}
```

Left-outer with possible nulls:
```ctl
//#CTL2
function integer transform() {
    $out.0.customer_id = $in.0.customer_id;
    $out.0.name        = $in.0.name;
    $out.0.region      = nvl($in.1.region, "UNKNOWN");
    return ALL;
}
```

## Examples

### Minimal — inner join: customers with payments (sorted by customer ID)

```xml
<Node id="SORT_C"   type="EXT_SORT"        sortKey="$customer_id(a)"/>
<Node id="SORT_P"   type="EXT_SORT"        sortKey="$customer_id(a)"/>
<Node id="JOIN"     type="EXT_MERGE_JOIN"
      joinKey="$customer_id#$customer_id"
      joinType="inner">
  <attr name="transform"><![CDATA[//#CTL2
    function integer transform() {
      $out.0.customer_id = $in.0.customer_id;
      $out.0.name        = $in.0.name;
      $out.0.amount      = $in.1.amount;
      return ALL;
    }
  ]]></attr>
</Node>
<Edge id="E1" fromNode="SORT_C:0" toNode="JOIN:0"/>
<Edge id="E2" fromNode="SORT_P:0" toNode="JOIN:1"/>
<Edge id="E3" fromNode="JOIN:0"   toNode="WRITER:0"/>
```

### Full — left outer join with reject port for unmatched master

```xml
<Node id="JOIN" type="EXT_MERGE_JOIN"
      joinKey="$customer_id#$customer_id"
      joinType="leftOuter">
  <attr name="transform"><![CDATA[//#CTL2
    function integer transform() {
      $out.0.customer_id = $in.0.customer_id;
      $out.0.region      = nvl($in.1.region, "UNASSIGNED");
      return ALL;
    }
  ]]></attr>
</Node>
<Edge id="E_OUT"     fromNode="JOIN:0" toNode="WRITER:0"/>
<Edge id="E_UNJOINED" fromNode="JOIN:1" toNode="UNMATCHED_WRITER:0"/>
```

## Common mistakes

- **Inputs not sorted.** No runtime check; output is silently wrong. Always pair with EXT_SORT (or trust upstream sort with explicit verification).
- **Sort key direction mismatched between EXT_SORT and joinKey.** EXT_SORT defaults ascending; if you set EXT_MERGE_JOIN's `ascendingInputs="false"`, the sort must match.
- **Slave duplicates ignored unintentionally.** `slaveDuplicates="false"` keeps only the last slave record per key — surprising when slaves intentionally have multiple rows per master. Default `true` is usually correct.
- **Transform not provided.** Required attribute; the component fails at validation if missing. Even pass-through joins need an explicit transform mapping fields.
- **Whole-record null check on a slave.** On left/full outer, test a concrete slave key field (`isnull($in.1.region)`), not the whole record (`isnull($in.1)`).
- **Confusing with `MERGE` component.** `MERGE` is k-way sorted merge of streams with same metadata — not a join. Different use case entirely.

## Notes

**Compatibility & deprecated attributes**

| Version | Change |
|---|---|
| 4.2.0-M1 | Second output port (port 1, unjoined master) added. Pre-4.2 graphs that needed unmatched-master capture had to re-engineer with a second join. Auto-propagated metadata for port 1 also dates from this version. |

Deprecated attributes (avoid in new code):
- `leftOuter="true"` / `fullOuter="true"` — pre-`joinType` toggles. Modern graphs use `joinType="leftOuter"` / `"fullOuter"` exclusively. The old toggles still parse but are silently overridden when `joinType` is also set.
- `errorActions` / `errorLog` — old "log and continue" mechanism. Removed in favor of per-record control inside the transform.
- `locale` / `caseSensitive` — pre-Unicode comparison knobs. Modern graphs rely on metadata-level locale settings instead.
- `ascendingInputs="false"` — works but rarely used in practice; consider sorting upstream rather than running merge-join descending.

      joinKey="$customer_id#$cust_id"
      joinType="inner"
      guiX="450" guiY="200">
  <attr name="transform"><![CDATA[//#CTL2 — see ## CTL2 contract]]></attr>
</Node>
```

- `type="EXT_MERGE_JOIN"`.
- Mandatory attributes: `joinKey`, `transform` (one of `transform` / `transformURL` / `transformClass`).
- Optional attributes: `joinType`, `slaveDuplicates`, `ascendingInputs`.
- `joinKey` notation — `<master keys>#<slave-1 keys>[#<slave-2 keys>...]`; each portion is a `;`-separated list of `$<field-name>`, optionally suffixed `(a)` (ascending) / `(d)` (descending). The direction suffix must match the input sort direction.
  ```
  $customer_id#$cust_id                               # field renamed in slave
  $first_name(a);$last_name(a)#$fname(a);$lname(a)     # composite, explicit ascending
  $customer_id#$cust_id_v1#$cust_id_v2                # one master + two slaves
  ```
- The CTL2 body is anchored in the `transform` `<attr>` CDATA.

## Properties

| Attribute | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `joinKey` | yes | — | Key expression. Format: master fields `#` slave1 fields `#` slave2 fields … (see `joinKey` syntax below). Number of master key fields = number of slave key fields per slave; the master key is shared across all slaves (same fields, possibly renamed). |
| `joinType` | no | `inner` | One of `inner` / `leftOuter` / `fullOuter`. |
| `transform` | yes | — | CTL2 (or Java) transform building the joined record. The Joiners transform template applies (see CTL2 contract). |
| `transformURL` | (alt) | — | External transform file. Use either `transform` or `transformURL`. |
| `slaveDuplicates` | no | `true` | When `true`, repeated slave keys all join with master. When `false`, only the **last** slave record at a given key is used. |
| `charset` | no | — | Encoding of the external `transformURL` file / inline transform source. |
| `ascendingInputs` | no | `true` | **Deprecated.** If `false`, expects inputs sorted in descending order. |
| `leftOuterJoin` | no | — | **Deprecated.** Use `joinType="leftOuter"` instead. |
| `fullOuterJoin` | no | — | **Deprecated.** Use `joinType="fullOuter"` instead. |

### `joinKey` syntax

`<master keys>#<slave-1 keys>[#<slave-2 keys>...]`

Each portion is a `;`-separated list of `$<field-name>`, optionally suffixed `(a)` for ascending or `(d)` for descending sort markers (must match input sort direction).

Examples:

```
$customer_id                                           # single-field, single-slave inner join
$customer_id#$cust_id                                  # field renamed in slave
$first_name;$last_name#$fname;$lname                   # composite key
$first_name(a);$last_name(a)#$fname(a);$lname(a)       # explicit ascending
$customer_id#$cust_id_v1#$cust_id_v2                   # one master + two slaves
```

Number of master key fields = number of slave key fields per slave. The master key itself is shared across all slaves (same fields, possibly renamed).

## Input & output metadata

Master (driver) on port 0, slave stream(s) on ports 1..n — each slave a separate input port with its own `joinKey` clause. The joined output is yours to define; the unjoined-master port mirrors port 0 and cannot be modified by the transform.

```
auto_propagated_metadata:   # joined output is yours; the unjoined port mirrors the master
  in.0:    <any — master / driver stream, sorted by joinKey>
  in.1..N: <any — slave stream(s), each sorted by its joinKey clause>
  out.0:   <you define — joined schema>   # transform() populates it
  out.1:   = in.0   # optional — unjoined master records (leftOuter / fullOuter only); pass through unmodified
```

A port-0 edge references your `<Metadata>`; the port-1 edge can ride the propagated master schema with no `metadata=` attribute.
- **Precondition — sorted inputs.** Every input **must** be sorted on its respective join key, in the same direction (default ascending). EXT_MERGE_JOIN does **not** verify the sort — if inputs aren't sorted, output is silently wrong. Common causes of failure: a `WHERE` clause that filters out the trailing portion of a sort, or a downstream step adding records out of order. Use `EXT_SORT` (or `FAST_SORT` for in-memory cases) immediately upstream; the `sortKey` of EXT_SORT must exactly match the corresponding portion of EXT_MERGE_JOIN's `joinKey`.

## CTL2 contract

Single entry-point function — the shared Joiners transform contract. The physical join strategy is sorted-merge; the CTL contract is identical across the join family.

```ctl
function integer transform()
```

**Call order / lifecycle:**
- `transform()` runs once per produced joined row.
- Return `ALL` to emit on port 0, an output port index to route, or `SKIP` to drop the row.

**Port model:**
- `$in.0` — master / driver record (port 0).
- `$in.1`, `$in.2`, … — slave records (ports 1, 2, …); null for left-outer / full-outer rows with no match.
- `$out.0` — output record.

**Idioms / keep in mind:**
- For `leftOuter` / `fullOuter`, guard slave-field reads with **field-level** null checks on a concrete slave key field, e.g. `nvl($in.1.region, "UNKNOWN")` or `isnull($in.1.region) ? "UNKNOWN" : $in.1.region`. Do **not** use whole-record checks like `isnull($in.1)`, and do not use sentinels (`-1`, `"NONE"`).
- Use fields from the correct port — slave-only fields read off `$in.0` cause field errors.
- Equality operators `==` and `!=` are null-safe; ordered comparisons on nullable values need guards.

**Minimal skeleton:**
```ctl
//#CTL2
function integer transform() {
    $out.0.customer_id = $in.0.customer_id;
    $out.0.name        = $in.0.name;
    $out.0.region      = $in.1.region;     // from slave 1
    return ALL;
}
```

Left-outer with possible nulls:
```ctl
//#CTL2
function integer transform() {
    $out.0.customer_id = $in.0.customer_id;
    $out.0.name        = $in.0.name;
    $out.0.region      = nvl($in.1.region, "UNKNOWN");
    return ALL;
}
```

## Examples

### Minimal — inner join: customers with payments (sorted by customer ID)

```xml
<Node id="SORT_C"   type="EXT_SORT"        sortKey="$customer_id(a)"/>
<Node id="SORT_P"   type="EXT_SORT"        sortKey="$customer_id(a)"/>
<Node id="JOIN"     type="EXT_MERGE_JOIN"
      joinKey="$customer_id#$customer_id"
      joinType="inner">
  <attr name="transform"><![CDATA[//#CTL2
    function integer transform() {
      $out.0.customer_id = $in.0.customer_id;
      $out.0.name        = $in.0.name;
      $out.0.amount      = $in.1.amount;
      return ALL;
    }
  ]]></attr>
</Node>
<Edge id="E1" fromNode="SORT_C:0" toNode="JOIN:0"/>
<Edge id="E2" fromNode="SORT_P:0" toNode="JOIN:1"/>
<Edge id="E3" fromNode="JOIN:0"   toNode="WRITER:0"/>
```

### Full — left outer join with reject port for unmatched master

```xml
<Node id="JOIN" type="EXT_MERGE_JOIN"
      joinKey="$customer_id#$customer_id"
      joinType="leftOuter">
  <attr name="transform"><![CDATA[//#CTL2
    function integer transform() {
      $out.0.customer_id = $in.0.customer_id;
      $out.0.region      = nvl($in.1.region, "UNASSIGNED");
      return ALL;
    }
  ]]></attr>
</Node>
<Edge id="E_OUT"     fromNode="JOIN:0" toNode="WRITER:0"/>
<Edge id="E_UNJOINED" fromNode="JOIN:1" toNode="UNMATCHED_WRITER:0"/>
```

## Common mistakes

- **Inputs not sorted.** No runtime check; output is silently wrong. Always pair with EXT_SORT (or trust upstream sort with explicit verification).
- **Sort key direction mismatched between EXT_SORT and joinKey.** EXT_SORT defaults ascending; if you set EXT_MERGE_JOIN's `ascendingInputs="false"`, the sort must match.
- **Slave duplicates ignored unintentionally.** `slaveDuplicates="false"` keeps only the last slave record per key — surprising when slaves intentionally have multiple rows per master. Default `true` is usually correct.
- **Transform not provided.** Required attribute; the component fails at validation if missing. Even pass-through joins need an explicit transform mapping fields.
- **Whole-record null check on a slave.** On left/full outer, test a concrete slave key field (`isnull($in.1.region)`), not the whole record (`isnull($in.1)`).
- **Confusing with `MERGE` component.** `MERGE` is k-way sorted merge of streams with same metadata — not a join. Different use case entirely.

## Notes

**Compatibility & deprecated attributes**

| Version | Change |
|---|---|
| 4.2.0-M1 | Second output port (port 1, unjoined master) added. Pre-4.2 graphs that needed unmatched-master capture had to re-engineer with a second join. Auto-propagated metadata for port 1 also dates from this version. |

Deprecated attributes (avoid in new code):
- `leftOuter="true"` / `fullOuter="true"` — pre-`joinType` toggles. Modern graphs use `joinType="leftOuter"` / `"fullOuter"` exclusively. The old toggles still parse but are silently overridden when `joinType` is also set.
- `errorActions` / `errorLog` — old "log and continue" mechanism. Removed in favor of per-record control inside the transform.
- `locale` / `caseSensitive` — pre-Unicode comparison knobs. Modern graphs rely on metadata-level locale settings instead.
- `ascendingInputs="false"` — works but rarely used in practice; consider sorting upstream rather than running merge-join descending.

name: Partition
type: PARTITION
description: N-way routing — routes each record to one output port via CTL2 getOutputPort() (not transform). The multi-port equivalent of EXT_FILTER.
tags: [component, flow, routing, partition, ctl2, fan-out]
scope: install
provenance: human-curated
sections: [description, purpose, xml, properties, ports, ctl, examples, mistakes]
---

# Partition

## Description

Routes each input record to exactly one output port chosen by a CTL2 `getOutputPort()` function. The N-port equivalent of EXT_FILTER (which is fixed at 2 ports). Use for routing by region, category, status code, or any per-record predicate that needs more than two destinations.

## Purpose & when to use

Reach for PARTITION when:
- You need to route to N (>2) output ports based on a per-record condition.
- The routing logic involves multiple branches, lookup tables, or computed expressions.
- Downstream branches need different schemas (each port can have its own metadata for the consumer, but PARTITION itself preserves the input schema).

Don't use PARTITION when:
- You only need 2 ports (pass / fail) → use EXT_FILTER (simpler, single boolean expression).
- Every record should go to every port → use SIMPLE_COPY.
- The routing is a hash-based balanced fan-out (not condition-based) → use balanced PARTITION modes or `executorsNumber` on the consumer.

## XML template

```xml
<Node id="PART0" type="PARTITION" guiX="400" guiY="200">
  <attr name="partitionSource"><![CDATA[//#CTL2 — see ## CTL2 contract]]></attr>
</Node>
```

- `type="PARTITION"`.
- The CTL2 body is anchored in the **`partitionSource`** `<attr>` CDATA — but the CTL2 function is `getOutputPort()`, **not** `transform()` (see CTL2 contract).
- One of `partitionSource` / `partitionURL` / `partitionClass` is **required** — see Properties.

## Properties

| Property | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `partitionSource` | yes* | — | Inline CTL2 holding the `getOutputPort()` function returning the integer port number for each record. |
| `partitionURL` | yes* | — | External `.ctl` file. |
| `partitionClass` | yes* | — | Compiled Java class. |
| `partitionKey` | no | — | Field name(s) to partition by — routes records to ports by key value (declarative alternative to a CTL2 `getOutputPort()`). |
| `ranges` | no | — | Value ranges used for range-based partitioning. |
| `charset` | no | — | Encoding for the `partitionSource` / `partitionURL` CTL2. |
| `locale` | no | — | Locale for string comparison when routing by key/ranges. |
| `useI18N` | no | `false` | Use i18n-aware string comparison for key/range routing. |

*One of the three is required.

## Input & output metadata

One required input; multiple outputs numbered 0…N, each record routed to exactly one. Metadata passes through on every port — define no `<Metadata>` on output edges; PARTITION routes, it does not transform.

```
auto_propagated_metadata:   # pass-through — output = input metadata (no transform to remap)
  in.0:  <any record metadata>
  out.0..N: = in.0   # each record goes to exactly ONE port (getOutputPort return value)
```

Edges out of PARTITION carry no `metadata=` attribute, e.g. `<Edge fromNode="PART0:0" id="E0" toNode="NEXT0:0"/>`.

## CTL2 contract

One entry-point function — **`getOutputPort()`, NOT `transform()`:**

```ctl
function integer getOutputPort()   // return the zero-based target port index
```

**Call order / lifecycle:** `getOutputPort()` is called **once per input record**; its return value decides the single target output port for that record.

**Port model:** one input (`$in.0`), multiple output ports. Routing only — **do not write `$out` fields** in PARTITION CTL (records are not transformed here, just routed).

**Return values:** a valid zero-based port index (`0`, `1`, `2`, …). A return value with no matching connected output port silently drops the record — always cover every branch with a catch-all `return N` for the highest connected port.

**Idioms / keep in mind:**

- You're generating a fixed or variable-length stream computed from sequences, parameters, or random functions.
- You want to fan records to multiple outputs based on the transform's return value (`return 0`, `return 1`, etc.).

}

    return SKIP;
}

### Minimal — random sales records

    $out.0.branch_id   = (sequence(SEQ0).next() % 10) + 1;
    $out.0.product     = randomString(5, 10);
    $out.0.quantity    = randomInteger(1, 50);
    $out.0.unit_price  = randomDouble() * 100;
    $out.0.sale_date   = today();
    return ALL;
}
]]></attr>

  <attr name="generate"><![CDATA[//#CTL2

    $out.0.branch_id   = (sequence(SEQ0).next() % 10) + 1;
    $out.0.product     = PRODUCTS[randomInteger(0, length(PRODUCTS) - 1)];
    $out.0.quantity    = randomInteger(1, 50);
    $out.0.unit_price  = randomDouble() * 100;
    return ALL;
}
]]></attr>
</Node>

<Node id="WRITER0" type="FLAT_FILE_WRITER"
      fileURL="${DATAOUT_DIR}/branches/branch_#.csv"
      partitionKey="branch_id"
      partitionFileTag="keyNameFileTag"
      outputFieldNames="true"
      makeDirs="true"/>

<Edge id="E0" fromNode="GEN0:0" toNode="WRITER0:0" metadata="Sales"/>
```

The `#` placeholder in the writer output path becomes each distinct `branch_id` value (`branch_1.csv` … `branch_10.csv`). One writer node, no PARTITION component, no manual N-port wiring. See `csv-file` § *Native file partitioning* for the full attribute reference.

Reach for the PARTITION component **only** when each output port needs a genuinely different downstream — different metadata, different transform, different sink type. Don't use it just to split into N similar files.

  <attr name="partitionSource"><![CDATA[//#CTL2

    return $in.0.branch_id - 1;  // route to ports 0..9
}
]]></attr>
</Node>

<!-- Then N writers, one per port — different per-port transforms if that's why
     PARTITION exists in this graph. If they all write the same shape to similar
     files, use the writer-side partitioning pattern above instead. -->
```

- **Forgetting output `<Metadata>`.** DATA_GENERATOR doesn't auto-propagate. Every output edge needs explicit metadata.

- **Expecting `$in.0` in `generate()`.** DATA_GENERATOR has no input port — generate from module state, constants, sequences, and random functions.

}
```

## Examples

### Minimal — random sales records

```xml
<Node id="GEN0" type="DATA_GENERATOR" recordsNumber="500">
  <attr name="generate"><![CDATA[//#CTL2
function integer generate() {
    $out.0.branch_id   = (sequence(SEQ0).next() % 10) + 1;
    $out.0.product     = randomString(5, 10);
    $out.0.quantity    = randomInteger(1, 50);
    $out.0.unit_price  = randomDouble() * 100;
    $out.0.sale_date   = today();
    return ALL;
}
]]></attr>
</Node>
```

### Full — fan-out to multiple files

Generate 500 records, distribute across 10 output files keyed by `branch_id`. The canonical CloverDX pattern is **writer-side partitioning** — one writer configured with a partition key and `#` placeholder in the output file path. PARTITION-the-component is **not** needed for fan-out by key.

#### Preferred — writer-side partitioning (one writer, N files)

```xml
<Node id="GEN0" type="DATA_GENERATOR" recordsNumber="500">
  <attr name="generate"><![CDATA[//#CTL2
const string[] PRODUCTS = ["Rose","Tulip","Sunflower","Lily","Orchid","Daisy","Carnation","Lavender"];

function integer generate() {
    $out.0.branch_id   = (sequence(SEQ0).next() % 10) + 1;
    $out.0.product     = PRODUCTS[randomInteger(0, length(PRODUCTS) - 1)];
    $out.0.quantity    = randomInteger(1, 50);
    $out.0.unit_price  = randomDouble() * 100;
    return ALL;
}
]]></attr>
</Node>

<Node id="WRITER0" type="FLAT_FILE_WRITER"
      fileURL="${DATAOUT_DIR}/branches/branch_#.csv"
      partitionKey="branch_id"
      partitionFileTag="keyNameFileTag"
      outputFieldNames="true"
      makeDirs="true"/>

<Edge id="E0" fromNode="GEN0:0" toNode="WRITER0:0" metadata="Sales"/>
```

The `#` placeholder in the writer output path becomes each distinct `branch_id` value (`branch_1.csv` … `branch_10.csv`). One writer node, no PARTITION component, no manual N-port wiring. See `csv-file` § *Native file partitioning* for the full attribute reference.

#### Alternative — PARTITION component (only when each output needs different logic)

Reach for the PARTITION component **only** when each output port needs a genuinely different downstream — different metadata, different transform, different sink type. Don't use it just to split into N similar files.

```xml
<Node id="PART0" type="PARTITION">
  <attr name="partitionSource"><![CDATA[//#CTL2
function integer getOutputPort() {
    return $in.0.branch_id - 1;  // route to ports 0..9
}
]]></attr>
</Node>

<!-- Then N writers, one per port — different per-port transforms if that's why
     PARTITION exists in this graph. If they all write the same shape to similar
     files, use the writer-side partitioning pattern above instead. -->
```

> The PARTITION node uses its own CTL2 contract (`getOutputPort()`), distinct from DATA_GENERATOR's `generate()`. See `partition`.

## Common mistakes

- **`recordsNumber` not set** — required attribute; CheckConfig fails.
- **Forgetting output `<Metadata>`.** DATA_GENERATOR doesn't auto-propagate. Every output edge needs explicit metadata.
- **Relying on `STOP` for a clean finish.** `STOP` stops generation but counts as an abort, not a graceful end. Control how many records are produced with `recordsNumber`; reserve `STOP` for advanced cases.
- **Random values per run breaking tests.** Set `setRandomSeed(42)` in `init()` for repeatable test fixtures.
- **Multi-port generation without metadata-per-port.** Each output port needs its own `<Metadata>` block; the transform's `return N` selects the destination.
- **Expecting `$in.0` in `generate()`.** DATA_GENERATOR has no input port — generate from module state, constants, sequences, and random functions.
